title: The Bosphorus Brief — 18 August 2026
overview: The big domestic story today is the official publication of the Terror-Free Turkey Process framework law, a significant legal development worth watching closely in the weeks ahead. Regionally, the US-Iran ceasefire has expired without a broader deal, and markets are jittery. Closer to home, the lira remains under pressure and Aegean tourism is feeling a pinch from regional tensions.

sections.heading: Terror-Free Turkey Framework Law Published
sections.body: The Framework Law on the Terror-Free Turkey Process has been published in the Official Gazette, confirmed by both CNBC-e and state broadcaster TRT Haber. SyriacPress carried commentary from Evgil Türker describing it as a breakthrough for equal citizenship, while columnist Ahmet Kepekçi raised questions in Yeni Mesaj about what shape the process will actually take. Separately, Kısa Dalga reports that MHP leader Devlet Bahçeli has referenced Abdullah Öcalan's 'conditions' and the European Court of Human Rights as possible agenda items — a detail residents interested in the broader legal and civil-liberties dimension of this process should keep an eye on. No changes to residency or foreigner-facing procedures have been announced alongside the law.

sections.heading: US-Iran Ceasefire Expires, Region on Edge
sections.body: The 60-day US-Iran ceasefire has lapsed with no broader peace deal, and President Trump has threatened action against Oman, according to MS NOW, The Hill, and The Telegraph. Equities fell and oil rallied on the news (Yahoo Finance). Turkey and Iran have been in direct talks about reopening the Strait of Hormuz and preserving the ceasefire, per Middle East Eye. For residents, there's no indication of direct disruption to Turkey itself, but it's worth watching flight and shipping routes through the Gulf if you have travel plans that way. Separately, a new poll cited by Al Jazeera and Middle East Eye shows US public concern rising over the broader Iran conflict, and Trump's approval has dropped to a new low.

sections.heading: Lira and Coastal Tourism Under Pressure
sections.body: Commerzbank analysts, cited by FXStreet and tmgm.com, say markets remain doubtful about Turkey's disinflation path and lira stability, with further depreciation expected against the dollar (USD/TRY currently 47.88). Turkey's July budget balance swung to a 378.1 billion lira deficit, reversing June's surplus (Bitcoin World). Meanwhile, Turkish Minute and the Financial Times report that regional tensions from the Iran situation, combined with last-minute booking patterns, have pushed down hotel prices along Turkey's Aegean coast and in Cyprus — a possible silver lining for anyone planning late-season travel, though it reflects softer demand overall.

sections.heading: EU Relations and Regional Diplomacy
sections.body: President Erdoğan said EU membership is 'no longer a priority' for Turkey, per eKathimerini, while separately calling for progress on the Customs Union and visa liberalization, which he described as being in everyone's interest (TRT Afrika, Anadolu Ajansı). Greece has meanwhile called Turkey's newly declared marine parks 'illegal,' a dispute covered by both euractiv.com and Daily Sabah — worth noting as one of several ongoing Aegean maritime disagreements between the two countries, reported with differing emphasis depending on the outlet.

closing: Stay dry, keep an eye on the lira, and check ferry and flight schedules if your travels take you toward the Gulf this week.
